SMTO-HTTP-0075 — SMTO reached the service, but the connection test didn't pass

GUID: e1c83338-f464-4262-a00e-cc5c2c79dd1b
Slug: http-connection-probe-failed
Domain: HTTP · Subsystem: http

What happened

  • SMTO's test request got an answer from the service, but that answer didn't confirm the connection works. The test only reads information, so nothing on the service was changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Parameter Store and select the HTTP Connection. Check that Base URL is the service's address and that Test endpoint under Connection test is a page that exists on it. The test asks for that exact page, so a wrong address or page returns an error instead of a confirmation.
  2. Check the Authentication settings, such as the username, password or token, against what the service owner gave you. Update them if they changed, then save. If the service doesn't accept the sign-in, the test fails even when the address is right.
  3. Select Test connection and note the result it shows, including the code from the service. That code tells you whether the problem is the sign-in or the address.

What success looks like

  • Test connection shows Reachable with the service's reply, and the task can use the connection.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the test result, to the person who runs the service or set up this connection. If someone else edited this connection, reload Parameter Store before changing it so you don't undo their changes.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The http.connect probe received an HTTP response from the configured test path that did not meet the connect success conditions, with no more specific error kind.

What this means

  • A connection probe returned an HTTP status but did not satisfy the connect success conditions and supplied no more specific error kind. The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.

Why this can happen

  • A connection probe returned an HTTP status but did not satisfy the connect success conditions and supplied no more specific error kind.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the public test path, status and complete/ok evidence before deciding whether routing or authentication failed.

How to fix it

  • Read status_code in the connect receipt: 401/403 points to authentication (retry_fields lists the credential slots), 404/405 to a wrong test_request url or method, and 3xx to base_url routing. Correct base_url, test_request or auth in the current saved HTTP profile, then run the probe again.
  • Check the public test path and authentication settings against the endpoint contract. Inspect the HTTP status before deciding whether authentication or routing needs correction.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • A documented read-only probe confirms the intended current connection.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
